methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Drones & Autonomous (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 7 same-sector peers exist in Drones & Autonomous, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Terra Drone, a Tokyo-listed public company in the Drones & Autonomous sector founded by Toru Tokushige, presents a valuation challenge due to limited comparable data. The sector universe comprises seven private peers—including Waymo, Wayve, Zipline, Joby Aviation, and Nuro—but no public comparables exist. This absence of listed companies at similar stage or valuation tier constrains traditional multiples-based analysis.

The Peer-Median method, the primary triangulation approach for early-stage technology valuations, is not applicable here. While seven same-sector peers exist, none satisfy the filtering criteria required for robust peer analysis: no peers match Terra Drone's public status or stage, and the valuation tiers across the private set are too disparate to yield meaningful median multiples. The analyst would require a minimum of three comparable datapoints at the same stage or valuation tier to generate defensible guidance, which the current dataset does not support.

Given these constraints, a valuation range cannot be triangulated from the provided data. The analysis exposes two key uncertainties: (1) the absence of Japanese or Asia-Pacific public drone companies limits regional market context, and (2) the wide dispersion in maturity and capital intensity across the private peer set prevents cross-sectional benchmarking. Supplementary data on Terra Drone's revenue, EBITDA, or growth trajectory—alongside public market comps or late-stage private funding rounds—would be necessary to establish a defensible valuation range.
